messages.subject: Multivariate Coefficients
parts:
Hi Everyone,

This is my first participation in the list. I was very excited when I read about Stan, some time I have been working with JAGS. But when I saw that Stan has a chance to work with matrix algebra within the code I decided to invest and am trying some simple models.

I read the manual but am having some problems with data structures, specially with the arrays of vectors. I would like any suggestions as to how to avoid the issue of the distribution multi_normal have a vector as input and only a vector!

Let me try to explain my situation: I have a data matrix Y[P,N] and incidence matrix X[N,T], my goal is to get the Ts coefficients of X for each column of Y (I call it alpha). So far so good, my code is working perfectly. However, I would like to model P vector with T coefficients following a multivariate normal. Other entry of my code are a matrix Omega[P.P] for priori of the variances and covariances between the P columns.

At this point I have problems, could someone give me a hand in creating the object that stores the coefficients for P adjustments so that respects the notation and I get them as multivariate?

Not found a guide posts, so I will send the code snippet. I Think that the data set is not necessary, but if someone need, I am currently avaliable. I hope that someone understand my question, and mainly my code. I am open for any suggestion!

Thank you for any help.

[CODE:]

data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=0> P;
  int<lower=0> T;
  vector[P] y[N];
  vector[T] X[N];
  // real means[P];
  // cov_matrix[P] Omega;
}
// transformed data {
//   real nu;
//   nu <- P * (P + 1) / 2;
// }
parameters {
  real<lower=0> s2[P];
  matrix[P,T] alpha;
  cov_matrix[P] G;
}
transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> s[P];
  for ( p in 1:P ) {
    s[p] <- sqrt(s2[p]);
  }
}
model {
  for ( p in 1:P ) {
    s2[p] ~ inv_gamma(10, 10);
    for ( n in 1:N ) {
      y[n, p] ~ normal(dot_product(X[n], alpha[p]), s[p]);
    }
  }
  // G ~ inv_wishart(nu, Omega);
  // for ( t in 1:T ) {
  //   alpha ~ multi_normal(means, G);
  // }
}

Best Regards,
FH

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Multivariate Coefficients
parts:
On 10/1/13 7:45 PM, FHRB Toledo wrote:
> Hi Everyone,
>
> This is my first participation in the list. I was very excited when I read about Stan, some time I have been working
> with JAGS. But when I saw that Stan has a chance to work with matrix algebra within the code I decided to invest and am
> trying some simple models.

JAGS and BUGS let you do some matrix algebra
in the models --- they just use an R-like syntax
for it.

> I read the manual but am having some problems with data structures, specially with the arrays of vectors. I would like
> any suggestions as to how to avoid the issue of the distribution multi_normal have a vector as input and only a vector!

You just need to make sure the type of the
data used in multi_normal is a (column) vector.

> Let me try to explain my situation: I have a data matrix Y[P,N] and incidence matrix X[N,T], my goal is to get the Ts
> coefficients of X for each column of Y (I call it alpha). So far so good, my code is working perfectly. However, I would
> like to model P vector with T coefficients following a multivariate normal. Other entry of my code are a matrix
> Omega[P.P] for priori of the variances and covariances between the P columns.
>
> At this point I have problems, could someone give me a hand in creating the object that stores the coefficients for P
> adjustments so that respects the notation and I get them as multivariate?
>
> Not found a guide posts, so I will send the code snippet. I Think that the data set is not necessary, but if someone
> need, I am currently avaliable. I hope that someone understand my question, and mainly my code. I am open for any
> suggestion!
>
> Thank you for any help.
>
> [CODE:]
>
> data {
> int<lower=0> N;
> int<lower=0> P;
> int<lower=0> T;
> vector[P] y[N];
> vector[T] X[N];
> // real means[P];
vector[P] means;

> // cov_matrix[P] Omega;
> }
> // transformed data {
> // real nu;
> // nu <- P * (P + 1) / 2;
> // }
> parameters {
> real<lower=0> s2[P];
> matrix[P,T] alpha;
> cov_matrix[P] G;
> }
> transformed parameters {
> real<lower=0> s[P];
> for ( p in 1:P ) {
> s[p] <- sqrt(s2[p]);
> }
> }
> model {
> for ( p in 1:P ) {
> s2[p] ~ inv_gamma(10, 10);

This should be pulled out of the loop and vectorized
to:

s2 ~ inv_gamma(10,10);

> for ( n in 1:N ) {
> y[n, p] ~ normal(dot_product(X[n], alpha[p]), s[p]);
> }

You should also vectorize this. You should be able
to get it down to a single loop:

for (n in 1:N)
y[n] ~ normal(X[n] * alpha, s);

with appropriate declarations. You want y[n], X[n] * alpha,
and s to all have size P.

This is faster, and if you're comfortable with linear algebra,
also clearer.

> }
> // G ~ inv_wishart(nu, Omega);
> // for ( t in 1:T ) {
> // alpha ~ multi_normal(means, G);

for (t in 1:T)
col(alpha,t) ~ multi_normal(means,G);

The function col() picks out column t of matrix alpha,
which is a vector. You need to define means as a vector,
too.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Multivariate Coefficients
parts:
On 10/2/13 4:37 PM, FHRB Toledo wrote:
...

> I agree with your points in regard to optimization, but I am trying first make the things work, and then make some
> optimization.
Absolutely the right strategy to pursue.

> Do you agree that if I work with the cholesky decompostion, according with the manual (multi_normal_cholesky()) to
> simulate multivariate normal could make the things fast?

If you use the covariance matrix more than once, then yes,
doing the Cholesky decomposition then using the Cholesky factor
should be faster. I don't think the difference is as dramatic
as it used to be because there's some caching going on internally.
So it's worth profiling with a few runs to see if it makes
a difference.

...

- Bob
